ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Maul.cs:40-43) == cost 1 / ATTACK / ANCIENT / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new DynamicVar("Increase", 1m)` (Maul.cs:34-38) == `_damage = 5` and `_increase = 1`; the hit count of 2 is a literal `WithHitCount(2)` in C# (Maul.cs:48) rather than a RepeatVar, and the sim stores it as `_hits = 2` so `base_hits` reports it -- a small improvement on the source, not a divergence.

OnPlay.rationale: Attack 5 twice, then buff EVERY Maul in AllCards by `Increase` (Maul.cs:48-57) == the sim's two-hit loop then `for card in ctx.player.all_cards: if isinstance(card, MaulCard): card._damage += self._increase`. The self-inclusion is right on both sides: C#'s `AllCards.OfType<Maul>()` includes the Play pile where the playing Maul sits, and the sim's `all_cards` includes the discard pile where the sim parks it (combat.py:452-454), so the card that was just played also gets the buff. Presentation, folded in: the NScratchVfx hit node.

AfterDowngraded.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- MaulCard has no downgrade hook, and `downgrade()` therefore DESTROYS the accumulated buff (maul.py)
AfterDowngraded.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `AfterDowngraded` EXISTS NOW. `Card._after_downgraded` (cards/base.py) is CardModel.cs:2150-2155, dispatched from `Card.downgrade` between the canonical rebuild and `Enchantment?.ModifyCard()` exactly as CardModel.cs:2144 does, and this card carries the override its C# does: a `_extra_damage` tally, kept as a CLASS default rather than an `_init_vars` line precisely because `_init_vars` is what the downgrade re-runs -- the mirror of C# holding it in a private field that `DowngradeInternal` does not touch. Pinned by test/test_downgrade_rebuild.py. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site; the seam's remaining residue is listed on creature_card_cmds/step52.  Maul's accumulation is per-PLAY and cross-card: `_buff_from_maul_play` (maul.py) is Maul.cs:72-76, where the damage bump and the tally are one statement, and OnPlay calls it on every Maul in AllCards (Maul.cs:51-56). Executed: an upgraded Maul played twice reaches 6+4 and downgrades to 5+4, where it used to drop to 5.  The text it replaced read: `AfterDowngraded()` calls base and then `DynamicVars.Damage.BaseValue += ExtraDamageFromMaulPlays` (Maul.cs:66-70) -- i.e. after `DowngradeInternal` has rebuilt the damage var from canonical (CardModel.cs:2140) it RE-ADDS the total this Maul has accumulated from Maul plays this combat, which the card tracks in a private field written by `BuffFromMaulPlay` (72-76). The sim accumulates into `_damage` directly (maul.py:306) and tracks nothing, so `Card.downgrade`'s `_init_vars` rebuild (cards/base.py:150-165) resets `_damage` to 5 and the accumulated increase is lost. Observable: play three upgraded Mauls (damage 6 -> 12), then have one downgraded -- the game leaves it at 5 + 6 accumulated = 11, the sim drops it to 5. LIVE: `downgrade()` is reachable from `powers.py:3171` (DampenPower downgrades every upgraded card in AllCards, IN COMBAT, which is exactly when the accumulation exists) as well as from `events/reflections.py:40` and `events/welcome_to_wongos.py:90`. This is a DIFFERENT downgrade defect from the five sticky-keyword cards -- there the flag survives when it should not, here a value is destroyed when it should not be -- so `card_probes.py downgrade` does not catch it: the probe compares a FRESH card against upgrade+downgrade, and Maul's loss only shows after a play. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): cards/base.py, CardModel.cs and powers.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: the buff is applied to all Mauls AFTER the attack, so this play's own damage is not increased (Maul.cs:48-57)
guards.rationale: The sim has the same order (maul.py:298-306): the two hits use the pre-buff `_damage`, then every Maul including this one is raised. Getting this backwards would make a single Maul deal 5 then 6.
